correctness.rationale: The increasing odd inter-square gaps make the earliest two marked positions of any multi-one factor uniquely identifiable by index k and left offset a. The exact preceding-square bound gives N_k. Reversed factors with at least three marks are impossible because strictly increasing gaps would reverse into a decreasing sequence. Reversal collisions for two-mark factors are precisely the unequal pairs of bounded external zero runs, giving an exact C_k formula. Case analysis for even and odd lengths proves the stated floor expression for every integer n >= 2, with n=0,1 handled explicitly. The even ordinary-complexity sum yields the asymptotic 2/3 ratio. Independently generated finite prefixes were exhaustively enumerated for lengths 0 through 100; separate finite gap-count comparisons hold to 2000; these are corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The nonnegative perfect-square indicator is a canonical arithmetic sparse binary word, and the newly introduced reflection-complexity measure motivates a complete exact evaluation. The result has nontrivial quadratic growth rather than the linear/automatic sequence regimes emphasized in the originating article; its leading ratio 2/3 to ordinary factor complexity has a structural reason from strictly increasing gaps and bounded reversal collisions. It resolves all lengths, not an arbitrary finite sample or computational exercise.
